messages:
ops-incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for Lyra (enterprise-vpc) — auth failures from 10.4.*/customer-traffic -> token introspection failing (500). impact: routing to dedicated pool failing for ~18% of requests. Automated severity: P1.
elaine: picking this up — on-call SRE. first check: is this an upstream (customer) auth issue or our JWKS fetch?
kevin: looking at proxy logs now. seeing a bunch of errors: 
```
level=error msg="introspection: jwks verification failed: no matching kid" path=/introspect tenant=lyra
```
Seems like the JWKS keys rotated on Lyra side and kid doesn't match. But timestamps show rotation ~20m ago, downstream started failing ~22m ago. suspicious.
maria: confirming: Lyra reported an internal cert rotation earlier today at 08:12 their local time. Sam (AE) says they did a quick rekey but might have omitted the old KID in the published JWKS. I've opened a ticket with Lyra infra.
tanya: two notes — 1) if we fallback to mTLS, check their client cert chain (we've seen incomplete chains cause TLS failures). 2) don't ask them to share private keys ;) we just need the proper JWKS endpoint and full cert chain if using client cert rotation.
jake: on the dedicated pool side, I've got logs showing TLS handshake succeeds but token introspection fails with 401 from our auth proxy when contacting lyra-jwks endpoint. cURL to their jwks URL returns 200 but payload only has new keys, old tokens still reference old kid.
elaine: mitigation plan options: A) request Lyra to reissue tokens (not feasible immediately), B) rollback to our cached JWKS (we keep last two snapshots for 24h) and accept tokens signed by old kid, C) add a transient allowlist route that skips introspection for a small percent and routes to a fallback model with strict quota to limit risk. thoughts?
kevin: we can re-enable cached JWKS for tenant lyra from S3 snapshot. quick command to pull snapshot: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-jwks-cache/lyra/2026-03-15T08:05:00.json /tmp/lyra-jwks.json
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @/tmp/lyra-jwks.json https://internal-config-api/reload-jwks?tenant=lyra
```
That would accept old kid-signed tokens again. downside: if Lyra intentionally removed key for security, we reintroduce a revoked key for a short window.
maria: customer impact: approx 18% of requests to Lyra private endpoints are returning 401/500; latency spikes for retries. They have a live revenue-critical pipeline (billing sync) hitting this. Sam — can you confirm tolerance?
sam_ae: Lyra says billing jobs can tolerate a brief window if we put a conservative rate limit and inform them; they prefer we use cached JWKS for now while they finish rotation. They estimate they can reissue tokens within 2 hours if we tell them to.
tanya: if we go cached-JWKS, add a compensating control: temporary signing-key expiration policy and alert if any token using the old kid is presented more than X times. Also enable verbose audit for lyra tenant.
jake: I can flip the cached reload and set an audit rule. Doing it now.
ops-incident-bot: runbook step executed by jake at 2795003100: reloaded JWKS snapshot and enabled tenant audit.
jake: done — JWKS rollback posted, audit rule set to log tokens using old kid to splunk index=auth_audit. See curl confirmation: 
```
POST /internal-config-api/reload-jwks?tenant=lyra -> 200 OK
```
elaine: monitoring — 2min after reload, 401 rate dropped from 18% -> 3%. errors still at 3% (likely tokens already expired). latency normalized.
maria: Lyra confirms their billing queue resumed and error rate is dropping. thanks team.
tanya: next steps: 1) coordinate with Lyra to complete rotation and publish JWKS with both keys for a TTL window, 2) add a small change to our JWKS policy: keep 48h of snapshots instead of 24h for enterprise tenants, 3) write a post-incident runbook section about JWKS KID-rotation detection and automated-safety (will add to runbook).
sam_ae: I'll schedule a joint call with Lyra infra in 30 minutes to confirm re-issuance and make sure their CI rotation script includes the previous key in JWKS for at least 1 hour.
elaine: also noting a secondary item we saw earlier in logs: occasional mTLS failures for a subset of Lyra hosts — looks like an incomplete intermediate chain was being served by one of their gateways. we asked them to re-concatenate certs (root + intermediates + leaf). quick verify command I sent them: 
```
# verify chain from our side
openssl s_client -connect gateway.lyra.example.com:443 -showcerts | openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
```
If they fix that it will reduce 502s for mutual TLS endpoints.
ops-incident-bot: severity downgraded to P2 at 2795004200 — main customer flow restored, still monitoring.
elaine: handoff to next on-call in 40m — I'll update the incident timeline and post a short summary in incident postmortems channel after full resolution. If Lyra finishes rotation earlier, set status=resolved.
kevin: I'll follow up to extend JWKS snapshot retention (PR ready) and add an alert on "sudden JWKS KID mismatch spike".
maria: final note for now: Lyra will notify when they've completed token re-issuance; keep this thread pinned to their support ticket.
sam_ae: on the call in 10. cc @Lyra_infra (external) — appreciate the quick collaboration.
elaine: thanks all — leaving a brief checklist in the postmortem: timeline, decision to reload cached jwks, mitigations, customer approval, and follow-ups on retention + detection. will hand off to oncall-sre rotation. :white_check_mark:
